Stated Claim / Post Context:
Early bird forecast for next Wednesday and Thanksgiving in Middle Tennessee

We'll be tracking a storm system over the southern United States.

Actual Article Body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WSMV) - Average temperatures are expected.

Just like that, 2026 is quickly coming to a close. Thanksgiving will be here next week, already. We’ll help you get prepared with this early bird holiday forecast, plus a look at next Wednesday — one of the busiest travel days of the year.

Next Wednesday, it’s likely a storm system will be traversing the southern United States. For now, it appears the most widespread rain will stay south of the Midstate, over the Deep South. That said, we still expect lots of clouds here with scattered showers.

For those traveling that day, if you’re headed toward Florida or the immediate Gulf Coast, it’s plausible you’ll run into more significant travel impacts from rain and road spray there than here.

Wednesday night, that storm system will slide farther east, taking the rain with it.

On Thursday (Thanksgiving Day), clouds will begin to decrease allowing sunshine to return. That means travel on Thanksgiving within a few-hour drive currently looks excellent. Locally, an afternoon break outdoors for a post turkey dinner walk should be very doable with a light jacket.

Temperatures should kick off the morning on Thanksgiving around 40°. Count on highs that afternoon to be in the mid-to-upper 50s. Nashville, traditionally one of the warm spots, should reach 60°.

Again, we’re more than a week away from the holiday, so expect changes to this forecast. We’ll keep you updated between now and then. Be sure to check back with the WSMV4 First Alert Weather Team for updates.

For life-saving weather alerts, customized messages on conditions and forecasts, and videos detailing upcoming weather events, download the WSMV 4 First Alert Weather app for iPhone or Android. Have weather pictures or videos? Share them here.
